Prelude header comment, verbatim: *"Modernist (dark) + the evreos shell skin. Every module value below is lifted from the real source: web/src/styles/modernist.css, components/Masthead.astro, CashbackBar.astro, AxisBar.astro and the cashback pages. The dark tokens are the derivation on the Palette artboard."*

## 6b. Palette board — the token table (light → dark → contrast on dark bg)

| token | light | dark | on dark bg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--color-bg` | `#f3f2f2` | `#201e1d` | — |
| `--color-surface` | `#eae9e9` | `#2d2b2b` | — |
| `--color-text` | `#201e1d` | `#f3f2f2` | **14.86** |
| `--ink-muted` 70% | 70% | 70% unchanged | 7.87 |
| `--ink-soft` 65% | 65% | 65% unchanged | 6.99 |
| `--border-strong` 55% | 55% | 55% unchanged | 5.41 /3 |
| link ink | accent-700 | accent-400 `#ff9783` | 7.91 |
| primary button | accent-700 / bg | accent-500 / `#201e1d` | 5.26 |
| focus ring | accent | accent unchanged | 3.95 /3 |
| `--color-divider` 40% | 40% | 40% unchanged | decorative |

Accent ramp judged on `#201e1d`: `accent-300 #ffc4b8` **10.94** *quiet ink* · `accent-400 #ff9783` **7.91** *links* · `accent-500 #ff563c` **5.26** *buttons* · `accent-600 #dd2b0f` **3.50** *refused* · `accent #ec3013` **3.95** *ring only*. Also named in the prelude: `--a200:#ffe0d9`, `--a800:#7c1405`, `--a900:#4d170e`, `--n800:#444141`, `--n200:#eae7e7`.

Palette headline: **"The dark theme was already in the ramps."** Body verbatim: *"The dark ground is the light theme's ink; the dark ink is the light theme's ground. Nothing new is invented — surface is `--color-neutral-900`, and the accent ramp `100…900` already exists. Radius stays `0`, Archivo stays `800`, and elevation follows the rule the stylesheet wrote for itself at `modernist.css:110` — a hairline edge and ambient darkness instead of a soft ink shadow."*

Two refusals, verbatim: *"`accent-500 on --color-surface` comes to `4.46 : 1` — forty thousandths under the floor, and invisible to the eye. It is why link ink is `accent-400` and not the step that looks right in isolation."* and *"`accent-600 as a button fill` comes to `3.50 : 1` against dark ink. The light theme fills buttons by going down the ramp to `accent-700`; the dark theme has to go up, to `accent-500`. Same gesture, opposite direction."*

The trap, verbatim: *"`contrast.test.ts` reads tokens with `css.match(new RegExp(\`${name}:\\s*([^;]+);\`))` — the **first** match in the file. A dark block that redefines the same token names under a media query would leave the gate quietly asserting the light values forever, green and meaningless. Whoever builds this either names the dark tokens distinctly or teaches the test about blocks first."*

## 6c. Theme board — the delivery chain

Headline **"One design, two grounds"**; body: *"The same screen, the same measurements, the same square corners. Only the tokens move. Nothing about the layout, the type ramp or the rhythm is theme-dependent, which is why this is a token swap and not a second design."* Captions: `light — ships today` / `dark — derived, not yet built`.

Chain: `OS / user setting` → `evreos` (*"Reads it, themes its own chrome, and passes it on. A shell-level switch may override the OS; that is evreos's to offer."*) → `theme.scheme` (*"Handed to every module over the bridge, with a change event so a mid-session switch does not need a reload."*) → `the module` (*"Honours it. Carries no switch of its own — one control for the whole app belongs to the shell, and two would disagree within a week."*) → `no bridge yet?` (*"`prefers-color-scheme` is the fallback, and it is the right one: it is the same OS setting, read directly."*)

Warning: **"The direction reverses"** — *"Light fills buttons and links by going **down** the accent ramp to `accent-700`. Dark goes **up**, to `accent-500` for fills and `accent-400` for links. Both clear 4.5:1. Reaching for the same step in both themes is the mistake that looks fine on one screen and fails the gate on the other."*

## 6d. Type, spacing, radii (derived from the shared prelude — no named `--font-size-*`/`--space-*` tokens exist)

**Fonts.** `--head:"Archivo",system-ui,sans-serif` loaded from `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Archivo:wght@400;500;600;800&display=swap` (weights **400, 500, 600, 800** only). `--mono:ui-monospace,Menlo,Consolas,monospace`.

**Headings.** `h1,h2,h3{font-weight:800;line-height:1.12;letter-spacing:-0.015em;margin:0;overflow-wrap:break-word;hyphens:auto}`. Body: `font-size:15px;line-height:1.55`.

**Type scale in use.** 44px/800/1 hero figure · 38px desktop h1 & board titles · 30px sign-in h1 · 28px mobile lead h1 / 28px `.figure` · 24px profile h1 · 22px wordmark (`letter-spacing:-0.03em`) · 19px mobile cell h3 · 15px body & primary CTA · 14–14.5px lede/extract · 13.5px section links · 13px `.btn`, `.rowline .k`, axis h6 · 12.5px seg-opt/chip/filter/`.rowline .v` · 12px field labels · 11.5px `.fine`, `.meta`, counts · 11px hero-kicker/`.owed b`/stat tags · 10.5px kicker/when/`.sec h2` · 10px `.tag`, rail labels 8.5px, tab labels 9.5px.

**Letter-spacing conventions.** `0.1em` uppercase eyebrows (`.kicker`, `.sec h2`), `0.08em` uppercase meta (`.host`, `.hero-kicker`, `.or`, `.owed b`), `0.06em` `.when`/figrow labels, `0.12em` `.d-figure span`.

**Spacing.** Mobile module gutter **18px**; desktop module gutter **24–26px**. `.pad{padding:22px 18px;gap:16px}` · `.sec{padding:15px 18px}` · `.row{padding:14px 18px;gap:14px}` · `.filter{padding:11px 18px}` · `.masthead{padding:12px 18px;gap:24px}` · `.d-masthead{padding:14px 26px;gap:18px}` · `.scell{padding:20px 24px}` · `.d-cell{padding:22px 26px}` · `.detail{padding:20px 24px}` · `.hero{padding:14px 18px 18px}` · `.btn{padding:10px 14px}`, `.big{padding:15px 16px}` · well `margin:10px;padding:9px`, desk-well `margin:12px;padding:10px`.

**Radii.** The module is `--radius: 0` — **no `border-radius` is set on any module element anywhere**. Rounding belongs to the shell only: `.well{border-radius:18px}`, `.desk-well{border-radius:20px}`, `.desk-top .addr{border-radius:15px}`, `.launcher`/`.fab`/`.rail .ri`/`.who-head .av` = `50%`, `.home i{border-radius:2px}`.

**Rules and elevation.** Section separator `1px solid var(--line)`; group separator `2px solid var(--line)`; emphasis box `2px solid var(--a500)`; shell dividers `1px solid var(--shell-line)`. Shadows exist only on shell chrome: `.launcher{box-shadow:0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,.55)}`, `.fab{0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.45)}` / light `rgba(20,20,30,.16)`. The module uses hairline borders instead of shadow (`modernist.css:110` rule).

**Frame sizes.** Phone `390×844` (boards override height for unrolled content: SignIn 920, Profile 886, Settings 1328, Merchant 916, Faq 1700). Desktop `1440×900`. `.osstrip` 44px, `.topbar` 48px, `.tabbar` 78px with a 5-col grid `1fr 1fr 84px 1fr 1fr`, `.home` 20px, rail 76px, desktop top bar 52px, master/detail `1fr 380px`.

# 7. Payout destination and opt-in — definitive answers

## Payout destination / bank details screen: **NO.**

No board draws a payout-destination entry form, a bank-details form, an IBAN field, or a verification flow. I grepped every board for `IBAN`, `SEPA`, `bank`, `Konto`, `τραπεζ`, `λογαριασμ`, `προορισμ`, `επαληθευ`, `destination`, `payout` — zero form fields anywhere. What exists is only:

| Board | What is drawn |
|---|---|
| `Settings.dc.html` | A `Πληρωμές` section with one read-only row: `Προορισμός πληρωμής` → `Δεν έχει επαληθευτεί`, hint `Η πληρωμή γίνεται μόνο σε λογαριασμό που σου ανήκει και έχει επαληθευτεί.` **Not a link. No screen behind it.** |
| `Profile.dc.html` | Same row + status chip inside `Η ανάγνωσή σου` |
| `ProfileDesktop.dc.html` | Same row + the requirement sentence `Η πληρωμή φεύγει από εδώ, οπότε ο προορισμός δεν μπορεί να ζει στον φλοιό.` |
| `AssistantDraft.dc.html` | A draft line `Προορισμός` → `Δεν έχει επαληθευτεί`, and a **withdrawal-confirmation phone** titled `Ανάληψη στον λογαριασμό σου` — which explains what happens next but collects no destination |
| `SettingsSeam.dc.html` | The ownership claim: `Payout destination — An account that is yours and verified. Money leaves through it, so it cannot live anywhere but with the module that moves the money.` |
| `WalletMobile` / `WalletDesktop` | A header status `Επαληθευμένο · οι πληρωμές είναι ενεργές` — the *verified* variant |

So the canvas asserts the requirement in three places and shows both statuses (`Δεν έχει επαληθευτεί` / `Επαληθευμένο`), but **the screen that would move a user from one to the other is a hole in the design.** That is the single largest gap the canvas implies.

## Opt-in / terms acceptance screen: **NO.**

Nothing on any of the 26 boards draws an opt-in, enrolment, participation toggle, or terms-acceptance step. Grepping every board's markup for `Ενεργοποί`, `Συμμετ`, `Όροι/όρους`, `αποδέχ`, `consent`, `terms`, `opt-in`, `participat`, `enrol` returns exactly three things:

1. `MerchantMobile.dc.html` — a secondary button labelled **`Όροι`** next to `Άνοιγμα καταστήματος`. That is a link to the merchant's terms, not an acceptance gate.
2. `Settings.dc.html` — the **consent-record** block, which is GDPR purpose consent (weekly email, anonymous reading stats, new-service notifications), **not cashback participation**. It is presented as a record ledger with `Ανάκληση` / `Παραχώρηση` actions, explicitly *"4 εγγραφές, όχι διακόπτες"*.
3. `SettingsSeam.dc.html` — `Consent records` assigned to the module (FR-011, `register.astro`).

The wallet and catalogue are drawn as though participation is already true — there is no "you are not participating yet" state and no gate before the first tracked click. Combined with `MerchantMobile`'s navigate-warning language echoed on `AssistantDraft` (*"opening a merchant writes a tracked click, which is a record with money consequences — so that one asks first, every time"*), the design implies a per-click confirmation but **never draws a one-time opt-in**.

---

### One naming note
The user-facing fixture brand on the boards is **`epiloYES`** (wordmark `epilo<em>YES</em>`, red `YES`) inside a host shell called **`evreos`**. **Zephyra** appears only once, on `LegalDesktop.dc.html`, as the legal-entity fixture: `<strong>Zephyra Fixture Koop…</strong>` under `Ταυτότητα` / `Impressum · TMG §5`. If you are building against a "Zephyra" brand, that is the legal-entity record, not the product wordmark.</result>

content.text: I have enough to resolve the blocking design decisions. Let me confirm three of them.

questions.question: The demo mints API tokens but has no Supabase project, so `make cashback-demo` cannot sign a *browser* in — its own closing message says so, and F8's browser test needs exactly that. How should a session be established locally and in CI?

options.label: Build the shell token-exchange, flag-gated (Recommended)
options.description: Build the design's second path now — a route that takes a JWKS-verified bearer token and mints a session of our own — behind an env flag that is off in production. The demo and Playwright turn it on; the shell *button* stays disabled with its copy until there is a shell. One mechanism serves the demo, the test, and production later.
options.preview:
POST /auth/shell   (enabled only when SHELL_TOKEN_EXCHANGE=1)
  body: token=<jwt from $TMP/reader.token>
  -> verify against JWKS_URL
  -> set our own httpOnly session cookie
  -> 303 to ?next=

production:  flag unset -> 404, button stays disabled
demo / e2e:  flag set   -> Playwright signs in in one POST

options.label: Point the demo at a real Supabase project
options.description: Give scripts/cashback_demo.sh real PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL / ANON_KEY for the nonprod project and use the true magic-link flow. Most faithful, but needs credentials in CI and a mailbox the test can read — the nonprod mailer is rate-limited.

options.label: A dev-only sign-in route
options.description: A separate route that exists only when APP_ENV is not prod, reading the demo's minted token. Simplest, but it is a second sign-in mechanism that production never exercises, so the path the test proves is not the path members take.

questions.question: F3's opt-in must render "the version and the document" of the terms. The brand carries `legal.documents.terms = {id, version}`, but no terms *text* exists anywhere — `lib/legal/strings.ts` has imprint, privacy and contact only. What should the member be accepting?

options.label: Add a /{lang}/terms route (Recommended)
options.description: A fourth pane in the legal family, written in el and de, rendering the cashback terms against the brand's entity and version. The opt-in states the essentials inline, cites the version, and links here. Nothing brand-shaped is a literal.

options.label: Inline summary, link to /{lang}/legal
options.description: The opt-in screen states in plain language what the member accepts and cites the version, linking to the existing legal page. No new route, but the cited document still does not exist.

options.label: Cite the version only
options.description: Opt-in posts the version and names it, with no document behind it. Smallest change; leaves the member accepting something unreadable.

questions.question: B4 — the edge sends every `/api/*` to the Go api, so the web's own `/api/cashback/clickout` is unreachable on Hetzner. Every Go route is under `/api/v1/`. How should F5 handle it?

options.label: Move the web's routes off /api/ (Recommended)
options.description: Rename /api/cashback/clickout and /api/tour/* to a prefix the edge never claims. Pure frontend change, needs no deploy coordination, works on previews and Hetzner immediately, and unblocks F5 now.

options.label: Wait for the edge matcher to narrow
options.description: Leave the web's routes where they are and let the deploy side change `@api path /api/*` to `/api/v1/*`. Fewer moving parts, but F5 cannot be proved on QA until that lands.

options.label: Both

### `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`on: pull_request, merge_group, workflow_call`; **no `push: main`** — `publish.yml` calls it on merge)

**`frontend`** (`defaults.run.working-directory: web`), verbatim steps:

```yaml

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
```


**`ts-types-drift`** — touches `web/`: regenerates `web/src/lib/database.types.ts` from a migrated Postgres 17 service container, then:
```yaml
      - name: Fail on drift between schema and committed generated code
        run: |
          git add -A web/src/lib

```

### `.github/workflows/migration-lint.yml`, `k8s-topology.yml` — not frontend-relevant.

### `commit-hygiene` specifics (job in `ci.yml`, lines 50–229)

Checkout is `actions/checkout@v7` with `fetch-depth: 0` **and `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}`** (the branch, not the merge ref — bug #494). Steps in order:

1. **Prove the checkout is the branch** — `git rev-parse HEAD` must equal the event's sha, else `::error::` + exit 1.
2. **Determine commit range** — `range=BASE_SHA..HEAD_SHA` on PR; `BEFORE..SHA` on a push with a real `before`; otherwise `$SHA -1`.
3. **Reject AI attribution trailers**:
   ```sh
   git log --format='%H %B%n----' <range> > /tmp/commits.txt
   grep -in -E '(co-authored-by:.*(noreply@anthropic\.com|claude)|generated with \[?claude|claude-session:)' /tmp/commits.txt
   ```
   A match fails the job.
4. `shellcheck -s sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh scripts/lint-commit-authors_test.sh scripts/lint-refs.sh scripts/lint-refs_test.sh scripts/pre-push-hook_test.sh .githooks/pre-push`
5. `sh scripts/lint-commit-authors_test.sh`
6. `sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh <range>` — checks **author and committer identity**, not just trailers.
7. `sh scripts/lint-refs_test.sh`
8. `sh scripts/pre-push-hook_test.sh`
9. **Reject a ref name that names an assistant or vendor** — `sh scripts/lint-refs.sh "refs/heads/$HEAD_REF"` on PR. Enforces **`xcoder/<slug>`**.
10. `sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages <range>`
11. **Require Conventional Commit subjects**:
    ```sh
    ^(feat|fix|chore|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|revert)(\([a-z0-9., /-]+\))?!?: .+
    ```
    on `git log --no-merges --format='%s' <range>`.

⚠️ **Local hooks are currently rerouted.** `.githooks/pre-push` and `.githooks/commit-msg` have been replaced by `entire` CLI wrappers that chain to `*.pre-entire`. The originals are `pre-push.pre-entire` / `commit-msg.pre-entire`. These files show as modified/untracked in `git status`. CI is unaffected but local enforcement is now indirect.

### **New browser/e2e tests: nothing exists and nothing would run them.**
No workflow installs a browser, sets up Playwright, or runs any `e2e` step. Adding browser tests would require a new job (and probably a `docker compose` service stack), plus adding the test files somewhere `vitest`'s `include: ['src/**/*.test.ts']` wouldn't pick them up incorrectly.

### How i18n works overall (it is a **per-surface catalogue** system, not a framework)

There is **no i18n library**. Each surface owns a TypeScript module exporting an interface plus one frozen object per language, and a `xStrings(lang)` selector:

| Module | Surface |
|---|---|
| `web/src/lib/reader/strings.ts` — `uiStrings(lang): UiStrings` | reader chrome |
| `web/src/lib/editorial/strings.ts` — `editorialStrings(lang)`, `languageName()` | editorial |
| `web/src/lib/legal/strings.ts` — `legalStrings(lang)` | Impressum / privacy / cookies |
| `web/src/lib/faq/strings.ts` — `faqStrings(lang)` | FAQ (sections → entries → answers) |
| `web/src/lib/member/strings.ts` — `memberStrings(lang)` | member sign-in |
| `web/src/lib/tour/strings.ts` | product tour |
| **`web/src/i18n/cashback.ts` — `cashbackStrings(lang): CashbackStrings`, `languageName(lang, subtag)`** | cashback member **and** operator |

`cashback.ts`'s header explains the placement rule: *"It lives under `src/i18n/` rather than beside the client because the cashback surfaces are the first in this frontend to need one catalogue across a member area and an operator area; `lib/reader/strings.ts` and `lib/editorial/strings.ts` each serve one."* **New cashback strings go in `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts`.**

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

      return Object.fromEntries(
        Object.entries(value as Record<string, unknown>)
          .map(([key, nested]) => [key, shape(nested)] as const)

    const walk = (value: unknown, path: string): void => {
      if (typeof value === 'string') { expect(value.trim(), `${path} is empty`).not.toBe(''); return; }
      if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null)
        for (const [key, nested] of Object.entries(value as Record<string, unknown>)) walk(nested, `${path}.${key}`);

    const walk = (value: unknown): void => {
      if (typeof value === 'string') { expect(value).not.toMatch(/€|EUR\b/); return; }
      if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null) Object.values(value as Record<string, unknown>).forEach(walk);
    };
    for (const lang of READING_LANGUAGES) walk(cashbackStrings(lang));
  });
  ...
});

describe('every interpolating string', () => {
  it('is exercised in both languages, so a broken template fails here', () => {
    for (const lang of READING_LANGUAGES) {
      const t = cashbackStrings(lang);
      const built = [
        t.entryCount(1, 2), t.entryCount(2, 2), t.shownInLanguage('Deutsch'),
        t.belowThreshold('10,00 \u20ac'), t.shortfall('2,00 \u20ac'),
        t.requestRecorded('WD-1'), t.reservedForRequest('18,40 \u20ac'),
      ];
      for (const line of built) {
        expect(line.trim()).not.toBe('');
        expect(line).not.toContain('undefined');
        expect(line).not.toMatch(/\$\{/);
      }
    }
  });
});
```

**Four hard constraints on every new cashback string:** (a) present in both `el` and `de` with identical key shape and depth; (b) non-empty after `.trim()`; (c) **contains no `€` and no word `EUR`** — money is formatted from `{minor, currency}` by `lib/cashback/money.ts`; (d) if it is a function, **you must add a call to the "is exercised in both languages" array** or the template goes unproven.

The same pattern (`carries every string in every alpha language (FR-015)`) is repeated independently in `legal/strings.test.ts`, `faq/strings.test.ts`, `member/strings.test.ts`, `editorial/strings.test.ts`, `reader/strings.test.ts`, `tour/strings.test.ts`. E.g.:

## 8. `.specify/memory/constitution.md` — constraints on frontend work

Version **1.3.0**, ratified 2026-08-14, last amended 2026-09-03. Path: `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\.specify\memory\constitution.md`.

### Principle VII — Language and Place Are Independent Axes (**verbatim**)

> ### VII. Language and Place Are Independent Axes
>
> A Greek speaker in Munich wants Munich news in Greek; that is the entire
> product thesis, and a single `el-DE` style tag breaks it. `language`
> holds BCP-47 primary language subtags only (the schema rejects combined
> tags), `place` is a self-referencing hierarchy, and articles and readers
> relate to places many-to-many. No code, schema or UI may fuse language
> and place into one locale value.
>
> This principle applies to every product. The cashback catalogue takes
> `lang` and `place` as separate parameters for the same reason.

### Rebrandability (**verbatim** — the brand-literal principle)

> ### Rebrandability
>
> - No product name, legal entity, domain, colour, logo, support address or
>   currency default is hardcoded in application code, templates or
>   migrations. All of it resolves from one brand configuration, and a CI
>   lint fails on a literal outside it.
> - All member-facing text lives in translation catalogues keyed by BCP-47
>   primary language subtag.
> - A fixture brand renders every member-facing surface in CI. Rebrandability
>   is a test that goes red, not a claim in a document.
> - Simultaneous multi-tenancy is **not** built. Forward compatibility costs
>   one brand id on the records where a tenant boundary would fall, and no
>   global brand singleton.

### Quality bar (**verbatim** — the testing principle that binds the frontend)

> ### Quality bar (both products)
>
> Go minimum 90% statement coverage and TypeScript minimum 80%, both
> CI-enforced; integration tests run against a real Postgres in CI;
> table-driven tests in Go; strict `golangci-lint` and clean `go vet`; every
> exported Go symbol documented. For cashback, a green coverage number
> without a passing C-1..C-7 invariant suite means nothing.

### Principle VIII (testing philosophy)

> Application code is never trusted with a legal guarantee. Every invariant above is enforced by the database … **Coverage numbers are necessary but not sufficient; a passing gate without these tests means nothing.**

### Other frontend-binding items

- **Architecture Constraints**: *"Frontend: **Astro** (v6+), TypeScript strict, `@astrojs/node` adapter."* Types generated from the schema (`supabase gen types` for TS): *"**Never hand-write types on both sides.** CI fails on drift."* — note `web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts` is a deliberate, documented exception (hand-written against the *HTTP contract*, not the schema).
- **Principle I** (NON-NEGOTIABLE): sole authorship, signed commits, Conventional Commits referencing an issue, one PR per issue, never commit to `main`, **every branch is `xcoder/<slug>`**, no AI attribution in commit messages, PR descriptions, **code comments, or documentation**.
- **Principle IX / C-6**: *"All monetary amounts are integer minor units with an explicit ISO-4217 currency code… **No decimal ever crosses an API boundary.**"* — `web/src/lib/cashback/money.ts` is described in `vitest.config.ts` as *"the C-6 boundary on this side of the wire"*.
- **Cashback alpha scope** includes *"Claim handling … a member may record a claim that a purchase did not credit, and an operator answers it with a named, permanent decision"* (C-8..C-10). **Out of scope for both products** explicitly lists: social login, referral bonuses, in-app spending of balances, member-to-member transfers, browser extension, mobile apps, search, comments — *"Do not build, do not scaffold, do not leave TODOs for"*.
- Governance: *"Every PR review verifies compliance: … **scope stays inside the declared product scope**"* — an absent surface must be refused by review.

## 10. MEMBER route contracts

Base path **`/api/v1/cashback`**. Every endpoint requires `Authorization: Bearer <Supabase JWT>` — *"there is no anonymous cashback surface (FR-023)"*. JSON UTF-8; errors are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457). Pagination: `limit` (default 20, max 100) + opaque `cursor`; lists return `{ items, next_cursor }`. **Money is always `{ "minor": <integer>, "currency": "EUR" }`** — no decimal ever crosses the boundary (C-6). Every mutating endpoint accepts `Idempotency-Key`.

```ts
// Money — the universal money shape (openapi components.schemas.Money)
{ minor: integer(int64), currency: string /^[A-Z]{3}$/ }   // both required
```

```ts

  type:   "about:blank",  // const; no problem-type URIs are minted for this API
  title:  string,         // HTTP status text, e.g. "Bad Request"
  status: integer,        // 400..599
```

⚠️ **The OpenAPI `Problem` declares NO extension members.** The contract prose (`http-api.md` L186–193) and `types.ts`'s `Problem` both promise `code`, `shortfall`, `threshold`, `confirmed`, `requested` as RFC 9457 §3.2 extension members on the withdrawal 409s. Palette headline: **"The dark theme was already in the ramps."** Body verbatim: *"The dark ground is the light theme's ink; the dark ink is the light theme's ground. Nothing new is invented — surface is `--color-neutral-900`, and the accent ramp `100…900` already exists. Radius stays `0`, Archivo stays `800`, and elevation follows the rule the stylesheet wrote for itself at `modernist.css:110` — a hairline edge and ambient darkness instead of a soft ink shadow."*

Two refusals, verbatim: *"`accent-500 on --color-surface` comes to `4.46 : 1` — forty thousandths under the floor, and invisible to the eye. It is why link ink is `accent-400` and not the step that looks right in isolation."* and *"`accent-600 as a button fill` comes to `3.50 : 1` against dark ink. The light theme fills buttons by going down the ramp to `accent-700`; the dark theme has to go up, to `accent-500`. Same gesture, opposite direction."*

The trap, verbatim: *"`contrast.test.ts` reads tokens with `css.match(new RegExp(\`${name}:\\s*([^;]+);\`))` — the **first** match in the file. A dark block that redefines the same token names under a media query would leave the gate quietly asserting the light values forever, green and meaningless. Whoever builds this either names the dark tokens distinctly or teaches the test about blocks first."*

## 6c. Theme board — the delivery chain

Headline **"One design, two grounds"**; body: *"The same screen, the same measurements, the same square corners. Only the tokens move. Nothing about the layout, the type ramp or the rhythm is theme-dependent, which is why this is a token swap and not a second design."* Captions: `light — ships today` / `dark — derived, not yet built`.

Chain: `OS / user setting` → `evreos` (*"Reads it, themes its own chrome, and passes it on. A shell-level switch may override the OS; that is evreos's to offer."*) → `theme.scheme` (*"Handed to every module over the bridge, with a change event so a mid-session switch does not need a reload."*) → `the module` (*"Honours it. Carries no switch of its own — one control for the whole app belongs to the shell, and two would disagree within a week."*) → `no bridge yet?` (*"`prefers-color-scheme` is the fallback, and it is the right one: it is the same OS setting, read directly."*)

Warning: **"The direction reverses"** — *"Light fills buttons and links by going **down** the accent ramp to `accent-700`. Dark goes **up**, to `accent-500` for fills and `accent-400` for links. Both clear 4.5:1. Reaching for the same step in both themes is the mistake that looks fine on one screen and fails the gate on the other."*

### `commit-hygiene` specifics (job in `ci.yml`, lines 50–229)

Checkout is `actions/checkout@v7` with `fetch-depth: 0` **and `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}`** (the branch, not the merge ref — bug #494). Steps in order:

1. **Prove the checkout is the branch** — `git rev-parse HEAD` must equal the event's sha, else `::error::` + exit 1.
2. **Determine commit range** — `range=BASE_SHA..HEAD_SHA` on PR; `BEFORE..SHA` on a push with a real `before`; otherwise `$SHA -1`.
3. **Reject AI attribution trailers**:
   ```sh
   git log --format='%H %B%n----' <range> > /tmp/commits.txt
   grep -in -E '(co-authored-by:.*(noreply@anthropic\.com|claude)|generated with \[?claude|claude-session:)' /tmp/commits.txt
   ```
   A match fails the job.
4. `shellcheck -s sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh scripts/lint-commit-authors_test.sh scripts/lint-refs.sh scripts/lint-refs_test.sh scripts/pre-push-hook_test.sh .githooks/pre-push`
5. `sh scripts/lint-commit-authors_test.sh`
6. `sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh <range>` — checks **author and committer identity**, not just trailers.
7. `sh scripts/lint-refs_test.sh`
8. `sh scripts/pre-push-hook_test.sh`
9. **Reject a ref name that names an assistant or vendor** — `sh scripts/lint-refs.sh "refs/heads/$HEAD_REF"` on PR. Enforces **`xcoder/<slug>`**.
10. `sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages <range>`
11. **Require Conventional Commit subjects**:
    ```sh
    ^(feat|fix|chore|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|revert)(\([a-z0-9., /-]+\))?!?: .+
    ```
    on `git log --no-merges --format='%s' <range>`.

⚠️ **Local hooks are currently rerouted.** `.githooks/pre-push` and `.githooks/commit-msg` have been replaced by `entire` CLI wrappers that chain to `*.pre-entire`. The originals are `pre-push.pre-entire` / `commit-msg.pre-entire`. These files show as modified/untracked in `git status`. CI is unaffected but local enforcement is now indirect.

### **New browser/e2e tests: nothing exists and nothing would run them.**
No workflow installs a browser, sets up Playwright, or runs any `e2e` step. Adding browser tests would require a new job (and probably a `docker compose` service stack), plus adding the test files somewhere `vitest`'s `include: ['src/**/*.test.ts']` wouldn't pick them up incorrectly.

### How i18n works overall (it is a **per-surface catalogue** system, not a framework)

There is **no i18n library**. Each surface owns a TypeScript module exporting an interface plus one frozen object per language, and a `xStrings(lang)` selector:

| Module | Surface |
|---|---|
| `web/src/lib/reader/strings.ts` — `uiStrings(lang): UiStrings` | reader chrome |
| `web/src/lib/editorial/strings.ts` — `editorialStrings(lang)`, `languageName()` | editorial |
| `web/src/lib/legal/strings.ts` — `legalStrings(lang)` | Impressum / privacy / cookies |
| `web/src/lib/faq/strings.ts` — `faqStrings(lang)` | FAQ (sections → entries → answers) |
| `web/src/lib/member/strings.ts` — `memberStrings(lang)` | member sign-in |
| `web/src/lib/tour/strings.ts` | product tour |
| **`web/src/i18n/cashback.ts` — `cashbackStrings(lang): CashbackStrings`, `languageName(lang, subtag)`** | cashback member **and** operator |

`cashback.ts`'s header explains the placement rule: *"It lives under `src/i18n/` rather than beside the client because the cashback surfaces are the first in this frontend to need one catalogue across a member area and an operator area; `lib/reader/strings.ts` and `lib/editorial/strings.ts` each serve one."* **New cashback strings go in `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts`.**

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

      return Object.fromEntries(

      if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null)
        for (const [key, nested] of Object.entries(value as Record<string, unknown>)) walk(nested, `${path}.${key}`);

      if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null) Object.values(value as Record<string, unknown>).forEach(walk);

    for (const lang of READING_LANGUAGES) walk(cashbackStrings(lang));
  });
  ...
});

describe('every interpolating string', () => {

    for (const lang of READING_LANGUAGES) {
      const t = cashbackStrings(lang);
      const built = [
        t.entryCount(1, 2), t.entryCount(2, 2), t.shownInLanguage('Deutsch'),
        t.belowThreshold('10,00 \u20ac'), t.shortfall('2,00 \u20ac'),
        t.requestRecorded('WD-1'), t.reservedForRequest('18,40 \u20ac'),
      ];
      for (const line of built) {
        expect(line.trim()).not.toBe('');
        expect(line).not.toContain('undefined');
        expect(line).not.toMatch(/\$\{/);
      }

```

**Four hard constraints on every new cashback string:** (a) present in both `el` and `de` with identical key shape and depth; (b) non-empty after `.trim()`; (c) **contains no `€` and no word `EUR`** — money is formatted from `{minor, currency}` by `lib/cashback/money.ts`; (d) if it is a function, **you must add a call to the "is exercised in both languages" array** or the template goes unproven.

## 8. `.specify/memory/constitution.md` — constraints on frontend work

Version **1.3.0**, ratified 2026-08-14, last amended 2026-09-03. Path: `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\.specify\memory\constitution.md`.

### Principle VII — Language and Place Are Independent Axes (**verbatim**)

> ### VII. Language and Place Are Independent Axes
>
> A Greek speaker in Munich wants Munich news in Greek; that is the entire
> product thesis, and a single `el-DE` style tag breaks it. `language`
> holds BCP-47 primary language subtags only (the schema rejects combined
> tags), `place` is a self-referencing hierarchy, and articles and readers
> relate to places many-to-many. No code, schema or UI may fuse language
> and place into one locale value.
>
> This principle applies to every product. The cashback catalogue takes
> `lang` and `place` as separate parameters for the same reason.

### Rebrandability (**verbatim** — the brand-literal principle)

> ### Rebrandability
>
> - No product name, legal entity, domain, colour, logo, support address or
>   currency default is hardcoded in application code, templates or
>   migrations. All of it resolves from one brand configuration, and a CI
>   lint fails on a literal outside it.
> - All member-facing text lives in translation catalogues keyed by BCP-47
>   primary language subtag.
> - A fixture brand renders every member-facing surface in CI. Rebrandability
>   is a test that goes red, not a claim in a document.
> - Simultaneous multi-tenancy is **not** built. Forward compatibility costs
>   one brand id on the records where a tenant boundary would fall, and no
>   global brand singleton.

### Quality bar (**verbatim** — the testing principle that binds the frontend)

> ### Quality bar (both products)
>
> Go minimum 90% statement coverage and TypeScript minimum 80%, both
> CI-enforced; integration tests run against a real Postgres in CI;
> table-driven tests in Go; strict `golangci-lint` and clean `go vet`; every
> exported Go symbol documented. For cashback, a green coverage number
> without a passing C-1..C-7 invariant suite means nothing.

### Principle VIII (testing philosophy)

> Application code is never trusted with a legal guarantee. Every invariant above is enforced by the database … **Coverage numbers are necessary but not sufficient; a passing gate without these tests means nothing.**

### Other frontend-binding items

- **Architecture Constraints**: *"Frontend: **Astro** (v6+), TypeScript strict, `@astrojs/node` adapter."* Types generated from the schema (`supabase gen types` for TS): *"**Never hand-write types on both sides.** CI fails on drift."* — note `web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts` is a deliberate, documented exception (hand-written against the *HTTP contract*, not the schema).
- **Principle I** (NON-NEGOTIABLE): sole authorship, signed commits, Conventional Commits referencing an issue, one PR per issue, never commit to `main`, **every branch is `xcoder/<slug>`**, no AI attribution in commit messages, PR descriptions, **code comments, or documentation**.
- **Principle IX / C-6**: *"All monetary amounts are integer minor units with an explicit ISO-4217 currency code… **No decimal ever crosses an API boundary.**"* — `web/src/lib/cashback/money.ts` is described in `vitest.config.ts` as *"the C-6 boundary on this side of the wire"*.
- **Cashback alpha scope** includes *"Claim handling … a member may record a claim that a purchase did not credit, and an operator answers it with a named, permanent decision"* (C-8..C-10). **Out of scope for both products** explicitly lists: social login, referral bonuses, in-app spending of balances, member-to-member transfers, browser extension, mobile apps, search, comments — *"Do not build, do not scaffold, do not leave TODOs for"*.
- Governance: *"Every PR review verifies compliance: … **scope stays inside the declared product scope**"* — an absent surface must be refused by review.

## 10. MEMBER route contracts

Base path **`/api/v1/cashback`**. Every endpoint requires `Authorization: Bearer <Supabase JWT>` — *"there is no anonymous cashback surface (FR-023)"*. JSON UTF-8; errors are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457). Pagination: `limit` (default 20, max 100) + opaque `cursor`; lists return `{ items, next_cursor }`. **Money is always `{ "minor": <integer>, "currency": "EUR" }`** — no decimal ever crosses the boundary (C-6). Every mutating endpoint accepts `Idempotency-Key`.

```ts
// Money — the universal money shape (openapi components.schemas.Money)
{ minor: integer(int64), currency: string /^[A-Z]{3}$/ }   // both required
```

### `GET /payout-destinations`

```ts

// PayoutDestination, additionalProperties: false
// required: [destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at]
{
  destination_id:  string /* uuid */,
  kind:            'sepa' | 'manual' | 'stub',
  verified_at:     string | null /* date-time */,
  verified_method: string | null,
  created_at:      string /* date-time */,
```

```ts

{
  kind:    'sepa' | 'manual' | 'stub',
  details: object,   // deliberately unconstrained; IBAN+holder for sepa, a note for manual
}
```

```ts
// OpenAPI components.schemas.Problem — required: [type, title, status]
{
  type:   "about:blank",  // const; no problem-type URIs are minted for this API
  title:  string,         // HTTP status text, e.g. "Bad Request"
  status: integer,        // 400..599
  detail?: string,        // omitted when nothing safe to say (notably 500)
}
```
⚠️ **The OpenAPI `Problem` declares NO extension members.** The contract prose (`http-api.md` L186–193) and `types.ts`'s `Problem` both promise `code`, `shortfall`, `threshold`, `confirmed`, `requested` as RFC 9457 §3.2 extension members on the withdrawal 409s. These are **not in `api/openapi.json`**. Treat them as optional/unverified when writing the frontend.

### `POST /api/v1/account` (B1, self-registration) — **TRULY ABSENT**

- `api/openapi.json` contains only `"/api/v1/account/tours"` (GET) and `"/api/v1/account/tours/{tour}"` (PUT). There is **no** `/api/v1/account` path and no POST.

Palette headline: **"The dark theme was already in the ramps."** Body verbatim: *"The dark ground is the light theme's ink; the dark ink is the light theme's ground. Nothing new is invented — surface is `--color-neutral-900`, and the accent ramp `100…900` already exists. Radius stays `0`, Archivo stays `800`, and elevation follows the rule the stylesheet wrote for itself at `modernist.css:110` — a hairline edge and ambient darkness instead of a soft ink shadow."*

Two refusals, verbatim: *"`accent-500 on --color-surface` comes to `4.46 : 1` — forty thousandths under the floor, and invisible to the eye. It is why link ink is `accent-400` and not the step that looks right in isolation."* and *"`accent-600 as a button fill` comes to `3.50 : 1` against dark ink. The light theme fills buttons by going down the ramp to `accent-700`; the dark theme has to go up, to `accent-500`. Same gesture, opposite direction."*

The trap, verbatim: *"`contrast.test.ts` reads tokens with `css.match(new RegExp(\`${name}:\\s*([^;]+);\`))` — the **first** match in the file. A dark block that redefines the same token names under a media query would leave the gate quietly asserting the light values forever, green and meaningless. Whoever builds this either names the dark tokens distinctly or teaches the test about blocks first."*

## 6c. Theme board — the delivery chain

Headline **"One design, two grounds"**; body: *"The same screen, the same measurements, the same square corners. Only the tokens move. Nothing about the layout, the type ramp or the rhythm is theme-dependent, which is why this is a token swap and not a second design."* Captions: `light — ships today` / `dark — derived, not yet built`.

Chain: `OS / user setting` → `evreos` (*"Reads it, themes its own chrome, and passes it on. A shell-level switch may override the OS; that is evreos's to offer."*) → `theme.scheme` (*"Handed to every module over the bridge, with a change event so a mid-session switch does not need a reload."*) → `the module` (*"Honours it. Carries no switch of its own — one control for the whole app belongs to the shell, and two would disagree within a week."*) → `no bridge yet?` (*"`prefers-color-scheme` is the fallback, and it is the right one: it is the same OS setting, read directly."*)

Warning: **"The direction reverses"** — *"Light fills buttons and links by going **down** the accent ramp to `accent-700`. Dark goes **up**, to `accent-500` for fills and `accent-400` for links. Both clear 4.5:1. Reaching for the same step in both themes is the mistake that looks fine on one screen and fails the gate on the other."*

| `SettingsSeam.dc.html` | The ownership claim: `Payout destination — An account that is yours and verified. Money leaves through it, so it cannot live anywhere but with the module that moves the money.` |
| `WalletMobile` / `WalletDesktop` | A header status `Επαληθευμένο · οι πληρωμές είναι ενεργές` — the *verified* variant |

So the canvas asserts the requirement in three places and shows both statuses (`Δεν έχει επαληθευτεί` / `Επαληθευμένο`), but **the screen that would move a user from one to the other is a hole in the design.** That is the single largest gap the canvas implies.

## Opt-in / terms acceptance screen: **NO.**

Nothing on any of the 26 boards draws an opt-in, enrolment, participation toggle, or terms-acceptance step. Grepping every board's markup for `Ενεργοποί`, `Συμμετ`, `Όροι/όρους`, `αποδέχ`, `consent`, `terms`, `opt-in`, `participat`, `enrol` returns exactly three things:

1. `MerchantMobile.dc.html` — a secondary button labelled **`Όροι`** next to `Άνοιγμα καταστήματος`. That is a link to the merchant's terms, not an acceptance gate.
2. `Settings.dc.html` — the **consent-record** block, which is GDPR purpose consent (weekly email, anonymous reading stats, new-service notifications), **not cashback participation**. It is presented as a record ledger with `Ανάκληση` / `Παραχώρηση` actions, explicitly *"4 εγγραφές, όχι διακόπτες"*.
3. `SettingsSeam.dc.html` — `Consent records` assigned to the module (FR-011, `register.astro`).

The wallet and catalogue are drawn as though participation is already true — there is no "you are not participating yet" state and no gate before the first tracked click. Combined with `MerchantMobile`'s navigate-warning language echoed on `AssistantDraft` (*"opening a merchant writes a tracked click, which is a record with money consequences — so that one asks first, every time"*), the design implies a per-click confirmation but **never draws a one-time opt-in**.

---

### One naming note
The user-facing fixture brand on the boards is **`epiloYES`** (wordmark `epilo<em>YES</em>`, red `YES`) inside a host shell called **`evreos`**. **Zephyra** appears only once, on `LegalDesktop.dc.html`, as the legal-entity fixture: `<strong>Zephyra Fixture Koop…</strong>` under `Ταυτότητα` / `Impressum · TMG §5`. If you are building against a "Zephyra" brand, that is the legal-entity record, not the product wordmark.</result>

input.content:
# Finishing the cashback member frontend (F1–F9)

## Context

`docs/master-prompts/cashback-frontend.md` on `origin/main` is the brief: bring
the member-facing cashback screens in `web/` to the point where one real person
can sign up, opt in, click out to a Linkwise retailer and watch a pending entry
appear in their wallet.

The backend is largely built. What the web cannot do is **sign a member in** —
`pages/[lang]/signin.astro` exists with every control `disabled` and says so on
its own face. Every cashback surface is already wired to an API it can never
present a member token to. Backend gaps B1–B6 (#544–#548) are being worked in
parallel; this plan builds against the documented contract rather than waiting
on them, and says explicitly which proof waits on which gap.

Three founder decisions taken this session:

- **Demo/CI sign-in**: build the design's second path — a route that exchanges a
  bearer token for a session of our own — behind an env flag that is off in
  production. The shell *button* stays disabled with its copy until there is a
  shell. The demo and the browser test use the route.
- **Terms**: add a `/{lang}/terms` route so the opt-in cites a readable document.
- **B4**: leave the web's routes on `/api/`; the deploy side narrows the edge
  matcher to `/api/v1/*`. Click-out is proved locally now, on QA when B4 lands.

## Starting state

`xcoder/member-signin` is **fully merged into `origin/main`** (PR #531) and ~30
commits behind it. Every branch below starts fresh from `origin/main`. The
working tree's modified `.claude/`, `.githooks/` and `.entire/` entries are local
tooling and are never committed.

**No issue exists for any of F1–F9.** Each PR below needs one opened first
(`gh issue create`), and dependent chains are bound with `gh stack`.

## What the survey established

**The auth seam already fits a member.** `resolveEditorSession(request, cookies)`
→ `editorSessionFrom(user, token)` → `{ displayName, email, role, token,
authenticated }`, filed in a `WeakMap<Request, …>` and read back synchronously by
`editorSession(request)` (`lib/editorial/session.ts:270–286`). There is **no
`Astro.locals` and no `App.Locals` type**. `roleOf` collapses anything that is
not `editor`/`operator` to `reader` — which is what a member is. `@supabase/ssr`
already exposes `signInWithOtp` and `verifyOtp`; **no new package is needed for
F1.** The middleware never redirects and does not match `/{lang}/signin`.

**`api/tour/[tour].ts` is the pattern** for a route that must keep a bearer token
server-side: it calls `resolveEditorSession` directly rather than trusting the
middleware to have matched its path.

**The design canvas** (26 boards, artifact `059a20a9-…`) draws SignIn almost
exactly as built — shell button primary, email link secondary, no password, no
"check your email" state. It **draws no opt-in screen and no payout-destination
form anywhere**; it asserts the payout requirement in three places
(`SettingsSeam`: *"Money leaves through it, so it cannot live anywhere but with
the module that moves the money"*) and shows both status chips, but never the
screen between them. Those two screens are mine to design. New screens use
`modernist.css`'s own tokens (`--space-N`, `--color-accent-N`, `--ink-muted`,
`--font-heading`), radius 0, hairline borders, no shadows — as `signin.astro`
already does.

**The contract has drifted, and it breaks a real screen.** Verified against the
Go source, not just the OpenAPI document:

| `types.ts` says | Go actually sends |
|---|---|
| `EntryState` = `…\|'declined'`, no `reserved` | `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` (`earnings/state.go:24–40`, migration 0013 check) — no `declined` |
| `PayoutDestination { id, kind, details, verified_at }` | `{ destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at }` — **and the Go comment says "There is no details field and there never will be"** (`payout/handlers.go:430–446`) |
| `Withdrawal { id, destination: {…}, reserved_amount }` | `{ request_id, destination_id, amount, state, requested_at, decided_at, decision_reason, payout_reference }` (`handlers.go:354–370`) |
| destinations/withdrawals paged | both are `{ items }` with **no `next_cursor`** (`handlers.go:385, 475`) |
| `Clickout.expires_at: string` | nullable |
| `Participation` has no `left_at` | `left_at` is required |
| `WalletEntry` | adds `merchant_name_language`, `merchant_name_is_fallback`, `hold_rule`; `merchant_name` nullable |

`withdraw.astro` renders `destination.details` and `reserved_amount`, and
`api.destinations()` unwraps a cursor page. **Against the real API the withdrawal
screen does not work today.** This is why the contract PR comes first.

**The member journey's other holes.** `api.optIn()` has zero call sites and
`t.optIn` is rendered nowhere; the wallet's not-participating band links to the
catalogue (`wallet.astro:242–249`). `participation()` is called only by the
wallet, so a non-participant is offered a click. Every member page collapses 401
into `503 + t.emptyQueue` ("nothing open in this list") through one broad catch.
`[slug].astro:82` reads `?clickout=<status>` with `.has()` and discards the code.
Only `rates[0]` is clickable. `next_cursor` is read nowhere. `CashbackNav.astro`
is dead code superseded by `MemberBar.astro`.

## The work

Each numbered item is one issue and one PR, several small commits, every
intermediate commit building and passing. Stacks are bound with `gh stack`.

### 0 — The contract, first *(unblocks everything that touches real data)*

`fix(web): the cashback types say what the api actually sends`

Correct `types.ts` against the Go handlers and `api/openapi.json`; make
`destinations()` and `withdrawals()` read `{ items }`; follow through into
`fixtures.ts`, the `entryStates`/`withdrawalStates` records in
`i18n/cashback.ts`, `withdraw.astro` and `wallet.astro`. This is a *correction*
to a hand-written file, not a contract change — the other two places already
agree. Open a **backend** issue for the one real contract gap: `api/openapi.json`
declares no extension members on `Problem`, while the prose and `withdraw.astro`
both rely on `threshold`/`shortfall` on the 409.

### 1 — F1, member sign-in *(a stack of five)*

1. `feat(web): a session resolves wherever a member signs in` — widen
   `isAuthenticatedPath` to `/{lang}/signin`, `/{lang}/register` and `/auth/*`.
   One mechanical commit renaming `EditorSession` → `Session` (it stops being an
   editor's), leaving `editorSession(request)` as the accessor.
2. `feat(web): the email link signs a member in` — a POST branch calling
   `signInWithOtp({ email, options: { emailRedirectTo } })`, guarded by
   `isSameOrigin` (`lib/csrf.ts:53`); a `/auth/confirm` route calling
   `verifyOtp({ token_hash, type })`, which writes the same `@supabase/ssr`
   httpOnly cookies the editor sign-in writes; a `?next=` return path accepting
   same-origin paths only. New `lib/member/strings.ts` copy for sent / expired /
   refused / not-configured, in `el` and `de`. `signin.test.ts` is **rewritten**:
   it asserts the working page as precisely as it now asserts the disabled one,
   and `member/strings.test.ts`'s "no URL, no `mailto:`, no `http`" rule is
   replaced with rules that fit copy that now describes a mechanism.
3. `feat(web): a signed-in member becomes an account` — after a successful
   callback, `POST /api/v1/account` with the member's own token (B1, #544).
   Until B1 lands that answers 404; the route records it and item 3 of F2 renders
   "your membership is being set up" rather than a 503.
4. `feat(web): the app shell exchanges a token for a session` — `/auth/shell`,
   present only when a new optional `SHELL_TOKEN_EXCHANGE` env field is set.
   **It verifies the token by using it**: one call to `GET /participation` with
   that bearer. A 200 or 404 means the api verified it against `JWKS_URL` *and*
   found an `account` row; a 401 refuses. That needs no JWT library (`jose` is
   not installed and this avoids adding it), cannot drift from the api's own
   verification, and proves membership rather than just signature. On acceptance
   the token goes into our own httpOnly `SameSite=Lax` cookie, read back by a new
   `lib/member/session.ts` resolver that tries this cookie first and falls back to
   `resolveEditorSession`. The shell **button stays disabled with its copy**.
   Record plainly that this session does not refresh — the shell re-hands a token.
5. `feat(web): sign-out, and the chrome that names who is signed in` — a sign-out
   POST mirroring the editor's; `MemberBar`'s `aside` naming the signed-in member;
   the front page's disabled button becoming a link, which retires
   `memberStrings.frontPageButtonState` and its assertion.
6. `feat(web): signing up is the same flow` — `register.astro`'s disabled account
   fields give way to the one email field; the consent panel is untouched.

### 2 — F2, gating

`feat(web): a cashback page without a member sends them to sign in`

One `requireMember(Astro)` used by every `/{lang}/{place}/cashback/…` page: no
session ⇒ redirect to `/{lang}/signin?next=…`; a 401 from the api ⇒ the same;
`/ops` without the operator role ⇒ a 403 page rather than chrome around an empty
queue. The broad catch stops collapsing 401 into `t.emptyQueue`, and gains a
member-facing error string of its own.

### 3 — F3, opt-in *(two PRs)*

1. `feat(web): the cashback terms, on their own route` — `/{lang}/terms`, a
   fourth pane in the legal family, rendering against `brand.legal` and citing
   `legal.documents.terms.version`. Nothing brand-shaped is a literal.
2. `feat(web): a member opts in before they can be paid` — a join screen reached
   when `GET /participation` answers 404, posting
   `brand.legal.documents.terms.version` — the same field
   `Participations.Join` compares (`internal/cashback/wallet/participations.go:162`),
   read from the same `brand.json`. `ErrNoBrand`'s 503 says the deployment names
   no brand and does not retry. The wallet's band points here, not at the
   catalogue.

### 4 — F5, click-out *(three PRs)*

1. `fix(web): the click-out failure says which failure it was` — read the status
   in `?clickout=<status>`; distinct copy for 401, 409, 429 and 502.
2. `feat(web): no click is offered to a member who has not opted in` — the
   merchant page checks participation, and the click-out endpoint refuses,
   until B3 makes the api refuse too.
3. `feat(web): every published band is clickable, not only the first`.

### 5 — F4 and F6, catalogue and wallet

1. `feat(web): the catalogue reads its next page` — `next_cursor` paging, plus
   the design board's ordering disclosure ("the order follows your language and
   your places; no position is sold"). The real endpoint arrives with B2 (#545);
   the fixture keeps development moving meanwhile.
2. `fix(web): the wallet's entry count stops capping at one page`.

### 6 — F7, payout destination

`feat(web): a member adds a payout destination`

`POST /payout-destinations` added to `types.ts`, `api.ts` and the fixtures
(`{ kind, details }` in, a destination with `verified_at: null` out); a screen to
add one; an "awaiting verification" state; `withdraw.astro:301–315`'s dead end
replaced by a link to it. Verification itself is B6 (#548) and is not needed
before the first transaction.

### 7 — F8, the end-to-end test

`test(web): the member journey, in a browser`

Playwright is greenfield — nothing in the repo or CI installs a browser. Tests
live in `web/e2e/`, outside vitest's `src/**/*.test.ts` glob, with their own
config and a new CI job. The test runs against `make cashback-demo` (which starts
Postgres-backed api, the JWKS stand-in minting `$TMP/reader.token`, and `astro
dev` on :4321) and signs in through `/auth/shell` with that token. It walks
sign-in → opt-in → click-out.

### F9 — carried by every PR

Every new string in `el` and `de`, satisfying `i18n/cashback.test.ts`'s four
rules: same key shape and depth, non-empty, **no `€` and no `EUR`**, and every
interpolating function added to the exercised array. Every new page literal-free
from its first commit — `scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh` is a per-file ratchet and
a file with no budget entry fails on its first hit. Every new logic module added
to `vitest.config.ts`'s coverage `include`, or it escapes the 80% gate silently.

## Files this touches most

- `web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts`, `api.ts`, `fixtures.ts` — the contract
- `web/src/lib/editorial/session.ts`, `supabase.ts`, `web/src/middleware.ts` — the session
- `web/src/lib/member/strings.ts`, `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts`, `web/src/lib/legal/strings.ts` — copy
- `web/src/pages/[lang]/signin.astro`, `register.astro`, and new `/auth/confirm`, `/auth/shell`, `/{lang}/terms`
- `web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/*.astro` and a new join screen
- `web/astro.config.mjs` — one new optional env field
- `scripts/cashback_demo.sh` — set the exchange flag so the demo's pages stop being fixtures

## Verification

Per PR, before pushing:

```sh
cd web && npm ci && npm run check && npm test && npm run build   # CI `frontend`
sh scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh                                # CI `brand-literals`
make ref-lint                                                    # xcoder/<slug>
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD
```

# Finishing the cashback member frontend (F1–F9)

## Context

`docs/master-prompts/cashback-frontend.md` on `origin/main` is the brief: bring
the member-facing cashback screens in `web/` to the point where one real person
can sign up, opt in, click out to a Linkwise retailer and watch a pending entry
appear in their wallet.

The backend is largely built. What the web cannot do is **sign a member in** —
`pages/[lang]/signin.astro` exists with every control `disabled` and says so on
its own face. Every cashback surface is already wired to an API it can never
present a member token to. Backend gaps B1–B6 (#544–#548) are being worked in
parallel; this plan builds against the documented contract rather than waiting
on them, and says explicitly which proof waits on which gap.

Three founder decisions taken this session:

- **Demo/CI sign-in**: build the design's second path — a route that exchanges a
  bearer token for a session of our own — behind an env flag that is off in
  production. The shell *button* stays disabled with its copy until there is a
  shell. The demo and the browser test use the route.
- **Terms**: add a `/{lang}/terms` route so the opt-in cites a readable document.
- **B4**: leave the web's routes on `/api/`; the deploy side narrows the edge
  matcher to `/api/v1/*`. Click-out is proved locally now, on QA when B4 lands.

## Starting state

`xcoder/member-signin` is **fully merged into `origin/main`** (PR #531) and ~30
commits behind it. Every branch below starts fresh from `origin/main`. The
working tree's modified `.claude/`, `.githooks/` and `.entire/` entries are local
tooling and are never committed.

**No issue exists for any of F1–F9.** Each PR below needs one opened first
(`gh issue create`), and dependent chains are bound with `gh stack`.

## What the survey established

**The auth seam already fits a member.** `resolveEditorSession(request, cookies)`
→ `editorSessionFrom(user, token)` → `{ displayName, email, role, token,
authenticated }`, filed in a `WeakMap<Request, …>` and read back synchronously by
`editorSession(request)` (`lib/editorial/session.ts:270–286`). There is **no
`Astro.locals` and no `App.Locals` type**. `roleOf` collapses anything that is
not `editor`/`operator` to `reader` — which is what a member is. `@supabase/ssr`
already exposes `signInWithOtp` and `verifyOtp`; **no new package is needed for
F1.** The middleware never redirects and does not match `/{lang}/signin`.

**`api/tour/[tour].ts` is the pattern** for a route that must keep a bearer token
server-side: it calls `resolveEditorSession` directly rather than trusting the
middleware to have matched its path.

**The design canvas** (26 boards, artifact `059a20a9-…`) draws SignIn almost
exactly as built — shell button primary, email link secondary, no password, no
"check your email" state. It **draws no opt-in screen and no payout-destination
form anywhere**; it asserts the payout requirement in three places
(`SettingsSeam`: *"Money leaves through it, so it cannot live anywhere but with
the module that moves the money"*) and shows both status chips, but never the
screen between them. Those two screens are mine to design. New screens use
`modernist.css`'s own tokens (`--space-N`, `--color-accent-N`, `--ink-muted`,
`--font-heading`), radius 0, hairline borders, no shadows — as `signin.astro`
already does.

**The contract has drifted, and it breaks a real screen.** Verified against the
Go source, not just the OpenAPI document:

| `types.ts` says | Go actually sends |
|---|---|
| `EntryState` = `…\|'declined'`, no `reserved` | `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` (`earnings/state.go:24–40`, migration 0013 check) — no `declined` |
| `PayoutDestination { id, kind, details, verified_at }` | `{ destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at }` — **and the Go comment says "There is no details field and there never will be"** (`payout/handlers.go:430–446`) |
| `Withdrawal { id, destination: {…}, reserved_amount }` | `{ request_id, destination_id, amount, state, requested_at, decided_at, decision_reason, payout_reference }` (`handlers.go:354–370`) |
| destinations/withdrawals paged | both are `{ items }` with **no `next_cursor`** (`handlers.go:385, 475`) |
| `Clickout.expires_at: string` | nullable |
| `Participation` has no `left_at` | `left_at` is required |
| `WalletEntry` | adds `merchant_name_language`, `merchant_name_is_fallback`, `hold_rule`; `merchant_name` nullable |

`withdraw.astro` renders `destination.details` and `reserved_amount`, and
`api.destinations()` unwraps a cursor page. **Against the real API the withdrawal
screen does not work today.** This is why the contract PR comes first.

**The member journey's other holes.** `api.optIn()` has zero call sites and
`t.optIn` is rendered nowhere; the wallet's not-participating band links to the
catalogue (`wallet.astro:242–249`). `participation()` is called only by the
wallet, so a non-participant is offered a click. Every member page collapses 401
into `503 + t.emptyQueue` ("nothing open in this list") through one broad catch.
`[slug].astro:82` reads `?clickout=<status>` with `.has()` and discards the code.
Only `rates[0]` is clickable. `next_cursor` is read nowhere. `CashbackNav.astro`
is dead code superseded by `MemberBar.astro`.

Each numbered item is one issue and one PR, several small commits, every
intermediate commit building and passing. Stacks are bound with `gh stack`.

### 0 — The contract, first *(unblocks everything that touches real data)*

`fix(web): the cashback types say what the api actually sends`

Correct `types.ts` against the Go handlers and `api/openapi.json`; make
`destinations()` and `withdrawals()` read `{ items }`; follow through into
`fixtures.ts`, the `entryStates`/`withdrawalStates` records in
`i18n/cashback.ts`, `withdraw.astro` and `wallet.astro`. This is a *correction*
to a hand-written file, not a contract change — the other two places already
agree. Open a **backend** issue for the one real contract gap: `api/openapi.json`
declares no extension members on `Problem`, while the prose and `withdraw.astro`
both rely on `threshold`/`shortfall` on the 409.

### 1 — F1, member sign-in *(a stack of five)*

1. `feat(web): a session resolves wherever a member signs in` — widen
   `isAuthenticatedPath` to `/{lang}/signin`, `/{lang}/register` and `/auth/*`.
   One mechanical commit renaming `EditorSession` → `Session` (it stops being an
   editor's), leaving `editorSession(request)` as the accessor.
2. `feat(web): the email link signs a member in` — a POST branch calling
   `signInWithOtp({ email, options: { emailRedirectTo } })`, guarded by
   `isSameOrigin` (`lib/csrf.ts:53`); a `/auth/confirm` route calling
   `verifyOtp({ token_hash, type })`, which writes the same `@supabase/ssr`
   httpOnly cookies the editor sign-in writes; a `?next=` return path accepting
   same-origin paths only. New `lib/member/strings.ts` copy for sent / expired /
   refused / not-configured, in `el` and `de`. `signin.test.ts` is **rewritten**:
   it asserts the working page as precisely as it now asserts the disabled one,
   and `member/strings.test.ts`'s "no URL, no `mailto:`, no `http`" rule is
   replaced with rules that fit copy that now describes a mechanism.
3. `feat(web): a signed-in member becomes an account` — after a successful
   callback, `POST /api/v1/account` with the member's own token (B1, #544).
   Until B1 lands that answers 404; the route records it and item 3 of F2 renders
   "your membership is being set up" rather than a 503.
4. `feat(web): the app shell exchanges a token for a session` — `/auth/shell`,
   present only when a new optional `SHELL_TOKEN_EXCHANGE` env field is set.
   **It verifies the token by using it**: one call to `GET /participation` with
   that bearer. A 200 or 404 means the api verified it against `JWKS_URL` *and*
   found an `account` row; a 401 refuses. That needs no JWT library (`jose` is
   not installed and this avoids adding it), cannot drift from the api's own
   verification, and proves membership rather than just signature. On acceptance
   the token goes into our own httpOnly `SameSite=Lax` cookie, read back by a new
   `lib/member/session.ts` resolver that tries this cookie first and falls back to
   `resolveEditorSession`. The shell **button stays disabled with its copy**.
   Record plainly that this session does not refresh — the shell re-hands a token.
5. `feat(web): sign-out, and the chrome that names who is signed in` — a sign-out
   POST mirroring the editor's; `MemberBar`'s `aside` naming the signed-in member;
   the front page's disabled button becoming a link, which retires
   `memberStrings.frontPageButtonState` and its assertion.
6. `feat(web): signing up is the same flow` — `register.astro`'s disabled account
   fields give way to the one email field; the consent panel is untouched.

### 2 — F2, gating

`feat(web): a cashback page without a member sends them to sign in`

One `requireMember(Astro)` used by every `/{lang}/{place}/cashback/…` page: no
session ⇒ redirect to `/{lang}/signin?next=…`; a 401 from the api ⇒ the same;
`/ops` without the operator role ⇒ a 403 page rather than chrome around an empty
queue. The broad catch stops collapsing 401 into `t.emptyQueue`, and gains a
member-facing error string of its own.

### 3 — F3, opt-in *(two PRs)*

1. `feat(web): the cashback terms, on their own route` — `/{lang}/terms`, a
   fourth pane in the legal family, rendering against `brand.legal` and citing
   `legal.documents.terms.version`. Nothing brand-shaped is a literal.
2. `feat(web): a member opts in before they can be paid` — a join screen reached
   when `GET /participation` answers 404, posting
   `brand.legal.documents.terms.version` — the same field
   `Participations.Join` compares (`internal/cashback/wallet/participations.go:162`),
   read from the same `brand.json`. `ErrNoBrand`'s 503 says the deployment names
   no brand and does not retry. The wallet's band points here, not at the
   catalogue.

### 4 — F5, click-out *(three PRs)*

1. `fix(web): the click-out failure says which failure it was` — read the status
   in `?clickout=<status>`; distinct copy for 401, 409, 429 and 502.
2. `feat(web): no click is offered to a member who has not opted in` — the
   merchant page checks participation, and the click-out endpoint refuses,
   until B3 makes the api refuse too.
3. `feat(web): every published band is clickable, not only the first`.

### 5 — F4 and F6, catalogue and wallet

1. `feat(web): the catalogue reads its next page` — `next_cursor` paging, plus
   the design board's ordering disclosure ("the order follows your language and
   your places; no position is sold"). The real endpoint arrives with B2 (#545);
   the fixture keeps development moving meanwhile.
2. `fix(web): the wallet's entry count stops capping at one page`.

### 6 — F7, payout destination

`feat(web): a member adds a payout destination`

`POST /payout-destinations` added to `types.ts`, `api.ts` and the fixtures
(`{ kind, details }` in, a destination with `verified_at: null` out); a screen to
add one; an "awaiting verification" state; `withdraw.astro:301–315`'s dead end
replaced by a link to it. Verification itself is B6 (#548) and is not needed
before the first transaction.

### 7 — F8, the end-to-end test

`test(web): the member journey, in a browser`

Playwright is greenfield — nothing in the repo or CI installs a browser. Tests
live in `web/e2e/`, outside vitest's `src/**/*.test.ts` glob, with their own
config and a new CI job. The test runs against `make cashback-demo` (which starts
Postgres-backed api, the JWKS stand-in minting `$TMP/reader.token`, and `astro
dev` on :4321) and signs in through `/auth/shell` with that token. It walks
sign-in → opt-in → click-out.

### F9 — carried by every PR

Every new string in `el` and `de`, satisfying `i18n/cashback.test.ts`'s four
rules: same key shape and depth, non-empty, **no `€` and no `EUR`**, and every
interpolating function added to the exercised array. Every new page literal-free
from its first commit — `scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh` is a per-file ratchet and
a file with no budget entry fails on its first hit. Every new logic module added
to `vitest.config.ts`'s coverage `include`, or it escapes the 80% gate silently.

- `web/src/lib/editorial/session.ts`, `supabase.ts`, `web/src/middleware.ts` — the session

# Finishing the cashback member frontend (F1–F9)

## Context

`docs/master-prompts/cashback-frontend.md` on `origin/main` is the brief: bring
the member-facing cashback screens in `web/` to the point where one real person
can sign up, opt in, click out to a Linkwise retailer and watch a pending entry
appear in their wallet.

The backend is largely built. What the web cannot do is **sign a member in** —
`pages/[lang]/signin.astro` exists with every control `disabled` and says so on
its own face. Every cashback surface is already wired to an API it can never
present a member token to. Backend gaps B1–B6 (#544–#548) are being worked in
parallel; this plan builds against the documented contract rather than waiting
on them, and says explicitly which proof waits on which gap.

Three founder decisions taken this session:

- **Demo/CI sign-in**: build the design's second path — a route that exchanges a
  bearer token for a session of our own — behind an env flag that is off in
  production. The shell *button* stays disabled with its copy until there is a
  shell. The demo and the browser test use the route.
- **Terms**: add a `/{lang}/terms` route so the opt-in cites a readable document.
- **B4**: leave the web's routes on `/api/`; the deploy side narrows the edge
  matcher to `/api/v1/*`. Click-out is proved locally now, on QA when B4 lands.

## Starting state

`xcoder/member-signin` is **fully merged into `origin/main`** (PR #531) and ~30
commits behind it. Every branch below starts fresh from `origin/main`. The
working tree's modified `.claude/`, `.githooks/` and `.entire/` entries are local
tooling and are never committed.

**No issue exists for any of F1–F9.** Each PR below needs one opened first
(`gh issue create`), and dependent chains are bound with `gh stack`.

## What the survey established

**The auth seam already fits a member.** `resolveEditorSession(request, cookies)`
→ `editorSessionFrom(user, token)` → `{ displayName, email, role, token,
authenticated }`, filed in a `WeakMap<Request, …>` and read back synchronously by
`editorSession(request)` (`lib/editorial/session.ts:270–286`). There is **no
`Astro.locals` and no `App.Locals` type**. `roleOf` collapses anything that is
not `editor`/`operator` to `reader` — which is what a member is. `@supabase/ssr`
already exposes `signInWithOtp` and `verifyOtp`; **no new package is needed for
F1.** The middleware never redirects and does not match `/{lang}/signin`.

**`api/tour/[tour].ts` is the pattern** for a route that must keep a bearer token
server-side: it calls `resolveEditorSession` directly rather than trusting the
middleware to have matched its path.

**The design canvas** (26 boards, artifact `059a20a9-…`) draws SignIn almost
exactly as built — shell button primary, email link secondary, no password, no
"check your email" state. It **draws no opt-in screen and no payout-destination
form anywhere**; it asserts the payout requirement in three places
(`SettingsSeam`: *"Money leaves through it, so it cannot live anywhere but with
the module that moves the money"*) and shows both status chips, but never the
screen between them. Those two screens are mine to design. New screens use
`modernist.css`'s own tokens (`--space-N`, `--color-accent-N`, `--ink-muted`,
`--font-heading`), radius 0, hairline borders, no shadows — as `signin.astro`
already does.

**The contract has drifted, and it breaks a real screen.** Verified against the
Go source, not just the OpenAPI document:

| `types.ts` says | Go actually sends |
|---|---|
| `EntryState` = `…\|'declined'`, no `reserved` | `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` (`earnings/state.go:24–40`, migration 0013 check) — no `declined` |
| `PayoutDestination { id, kind, details, verified_at }` | `{ destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at }` — **and the Go comment says "There is no details field and there never will be"** (`payout/handlers.go:430–446`) |
| `Withdrawal { id, destination: {…}, reserved_amount }` | `{ request_id, destination_id, amount, state, requested_at, decided_at, decision_reason, payout_reference }` (`handlers.go:354–370`) |

`api.destinations()` unwraps a cursor page. **Against the real API the withdrawal

appear in their wallet.

parallel; this plan builds against the documented contract rather than waiting
on them, and says explicitly which proof waits on which gap.

Three founder decisions taken this session:

  bearer token for a session of our own — behind an env flag that is off in
  production. The shell *button* stays disabled with its copy until there is a
  shell. The demo and the browser test use the route.
- **Terms**: add a `/{lang}/terms` route so the opt-in cites a readable document.

  matcher to `/api/v1/*`. Click-out is proved locally now, on QA when B4 lands.

`xcoder/member-signin` is **fully merged into `origin/main`** (PR #531) and ~30

middleware to have matched its path.

**The design canvas** (26 boards, artifact `059a20a9-…`) draws SignIn almost

form anywhere**; it asserts the payout requirement in three places

5. `feat(web): sign-out, and the chrome that names who is signed in` — a sign-out
   POST mirroring the editor's; `MemberBar`'s `aside` naming the signed-in member;
   the front page's disabled button becoming a link, which retires
   `memberStrings.frontPageButtonState` and its assertion.
6. `feat(web): signing up is the same flow` — `register.astro`'s disabled account
   fields give way to the one email field; the consent panel is untouched.

### 2 — F2, gating

`feat(web): a cashback page without a member sends them to sign in`

One `requireMember(Astro)` used by every `/{lang}/{place}/cashback/…` page: no
session ⇒ redirect to `/{lang}/signin?next=…`; a 401 from the api ⇒ the same;
`/ops` without the operator role ⇒ a 403 page rather than chrome around an empty
queue. The broad catch stops collapsing 401 into `t.emptyQueue`, and gains a
member-facing error string of its own.

### 3 — F3, opt-in *(two PRs)*

1. `feat(web): the cashback terms, on their own route` — `/{lang}/terms`, a
   fourth pane in the legal family, rendering against `brand.legal` and citing
   `legal.documents.terms.version`. Nothing brand-shaped is a literal.
2. `feat(web): a member opts in before they can be paid` — a join screen reached
   when `GET /participation` answers 404, posting
   `brand.legal.documents.terms.version` — the same field
   `Participations.Join` compares (`internal/cashback/wallet/participations.go:162`),
   read from the same `brand.json`. `ErrNoBrand`'s 503 says the deployment names
   no brand and does not retry. The wallet's band points here, not at the
   catalogue.

### 4 — F5, click-out *(three PRs)*

1. `fix(web): the click-out failure says which failure it was` — read the status
   in `?clickout=<status>`; distinct copy for 401, 409, 429 and 502.
2. `feat(web): no click is offered to a member who has not opted in` — the
   merchant page checks participation, and the click-out endpoint refuses,
   until B3 makes the api refuse too.
3. `feat(web): every published band is clickable, not only the first`.

### 5 — F4 and F6, catalogue and wallet

1. `feat(web): the catalogue reads its next page` — `next_cursor` paging, plus
   the design board's ordering disclosure ("the order follows your language and
   your places; no position is sold"). The real endpoint arrives with B2 (#545);
   the fixture keeps development moving meanwhile.
2. `fix(web): the wallet's entry count stops capping at one page`.

### 6 — F7, payout destination

`feat(web): a member adds a payout destination`

`POST /payout-destinations` added to `types.ts`, `api.ts` and the fixtures
(`{ kind, details }` in, a destination with `verified_at: null` out); a screen to
add one; an "awaiting verification" state; `withdraw.astro:301–315`'s dead end
replaced by a link to it. Verification itself is B6 (#548) and is not needed
before the first transaction.

### 7 — F8, the end-to-end test

`test(web): the member journey, in a browser`

Playwright is greenfield — nothing in the repo or CI installs a browser. Tests
live in `web/e2e/`, outside vitest's `src/**/*.test.ts` glob, with their own
config and a new CI job. The test runs against `make cashback-demo` (which starts
Postgres-backed api, the JWKS stand-in minting `$TMP/reader.token`, and `astro
dev` on :4321) and signs in through `/auth/shell` with that token. It walks
sign-in → opt-in → click-out.

Every new string in `el` and `de`, satisfying `i18n/cashback.test.ts`'s four
rules: same key shape and depth, non-empty, **no `€` and no `EUR`**, and every
interpolating function added to the exercised array. Every new page literal-free
from its first commit — `scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh` is a per-file ratchet and
a file with no budget entry fails on its first hit. Every new logic module added
to `vitest.config.ts`'s coverage `include`, or it escapes the 80% gate silently.
